# Error

Error handling statement to force an error to be generated

## Syntax

```freebasic
Declare Sub Error ( errno As Long )
```

## Parameters

- `number`

## Description

**Error** invokes the error handler specified with [On Error](On-Error) or, in case there was none set, aborts the program, printing an error message similar to those generated by the compiler's -exx run-time error checking. It's possible to use the [built-in run-time error numbers](Runtime-Error-Codes) and/or other custom error numbers for *number*. This can be used to simulate custom error numbers.

## Remarks

### Usage

`Error number`

### Differences from QB

- Error numbers are not the same as in QB.

### See also

- [`Err`](Err)
- [Error Handling](Error-Handling)
- [Runtime Error Codes](Runtime-Error-Codes)

## Examples

To send an error alert of error 150 (just some arbitrary error code) one would do the following:

`Error 150`
